name: Quantitative Verification
description:
The course teaches the fundamentals of modelling and analysis
of systems featuring quantitative behaviour, such as time and
probabilities. Topics include:
- Representation of hardware and software systems using formal models
of computations, e.g., transition systems, discrete-time and
continuous-time Markov chains, Markov decision processes, stochastic
games, timed automata.
- Representation of specifications using formal logics, e.g.,
probabilistic linear temporal logic, probabilistic computation-tree
logic, continuous stochastic logic, metric temporal logic.
- Algorithms for various classes of formal models and specifications,
e.g., transient analysis, stationary analysis, mean-payoff
optimization, reachability-game solving.
- Theoretically optimal as well as practical techniques for analysis
of large systems, e.g., linear programming, value iteration, strategy
iteration, reinforcement learning.
- Industrial application of the analysis, e.g., randomised
communication protocols, embedded systems, cyber-physical systems,
safety-critical missions.
- Practical experience in applying model checking tools, e.g., PRISM,
MRMC, UPPAAL.
prerequisites:
Prerequisites: IN0011 Einführung in die Theoretische Informatik,
IN0015 Diskrete Strukturen, IN0018 Diskrete Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie
